name: King of the Mat 2

date.source: The broadcast's own dating ("April 4th" is given inside the show's own opening narration as an in-story date, but the posted parts are dated and framed as the night of 6 April 1998 on rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy); a follow-up N.E.W. post several weeks later cites this event as "King of the Mat 2" on that date.

appearances.note: Won the night's ten-man King of the Mat tournament (not individually structured into matches[]), earning a N.E.W. Heavyweight Championship shot at the promotion's next pay-per-view.

matches.stipulation: N.E.W. Tag Team Championship Tournament Final
matches.note: The Crash Test Dummies became the new, Undisputed N.E.W. Tag Team Champions after their opponents' own teamwork broke down.

An initial disqualification finish was overturned on-air by N.E.W. official Ima Blindman, who ordered the match restarted; Miller retained after an ally known only as the Masked Man clipped Snyder's knee from outside.

matches.stipulation: Crucifix Match for the N.E.W. Intercontinental Championship
matches.note: Jacobs, aided from outside by stablemate Jim Whitten, tied Balial to a crucifix suspended above the ring for the win; new champion.
Ended without a fall after Steve Miller's manager Monica interfered; both women's ringside partners ran in to cover them and end the segment.

Levavy retained; afterward, a masked "Desire" Brandon Bloom and stablemates Steve Miller, Tommy Shaw, and "Kodiac" Dan Harris beat down the unconscious champion and revealed themselves as a new faction, later known as the Fellas.

notes: The night's ten-man King of the Mat tournament, won by James Pillow, is attested by the served page's own text but not individually structured into matches[].

name: Friday Night Slam Dance

date.source: The show's own on-air narration dates it explicitly; the posting author's own follow-up correction post confirms 24 April 1998 after two of the five parts' own subject lines misdated it.

appearances.note: Turned on his own New Wave Society stable mid-match, revealing a Too Extreme (2EX) t-shirt underneath his own gear, and joined that stable.
Suffered an in-match knee injury and was eliminated first, then taken out on a stretcher.
Won the N.E.W. Heavyweight Championship and aligned with the debuting Fab Five stable.
Named on-air as the reigning N.E.W. Tag Team Champions.

Struck James Pillow with the championship belt to set up Vinny Vitrone's title win, then announced the stable's rebrand from the Fellas to the Fab Five, naming himself the reigning N.E.W. North American Champion.

matches.note: GlacierIce won after New Wave Society stablemate "the Iceman" Chris Lethbridge slipped him a pair of brass knuckles; the match had briefly been called for Tank on an early bell before being restarted.
Ended without a finish when Walsh turned on his own stable mid-match to join Too Extreme (2EX), the champion's own faction.

matches.stipulation: N.E.W. Heavyweight Championship, Four Way Dance
matches.note: Levavy was eliminated first (knee injury) and taken out on a stretcher; Brass Knuckles was eliminated next. Vitrone pinned Pillow for the title after stablemate Steve Miller struck Pillow with the championship belt. New champion; the debuting stable renamed itself from the Fellas to the Fab Five afterward.

notes: This show also carries the on-air announcement of President GoodFella's retirement and the transfer of the promotion's front office to co-Presidents Bob Wilhem and Mark Mitchell and Executive Consultant Brandon Bloom — an administrative angle, not structured into appearances[]/matches[].
